checks: Actual frontend applies explicit FileSync replies after a missed patch and resumes incremental updates
FileSync recovery cannot resurrect closed documents, overwrite a switched project or replace a newer document identity
Missed-patch snapshots preserve pending text for conflict review and ignore duplicate or older revisions
Own patch acknowledgements and late legacy snapshots retain newer local typing without false own attribution
Actual frontend patch generation preserves Unicode scalar boundaries for astral replacements
A newly recovered host snapshot frees a known equal acknowledged device draft without deleting unknown storage
Peer snapshots and patches before the first IME input retain the original base and defer marked selection and conflict focus
Canceled or no-change IME does not fabricate an old-source draft over a newer peer snapshot
A verified own acknowledgement safely rebases a composing pending source without treating a foreign snapshot as its acknowledgement
IME commits stay with their captured document across disconnects, remote close, deferred selection and a new project identity
A flush already awaiting acknowledgement cannot send marked text when composition starts during its wait
A disk conflict arriving during a canceled composition is shown only after marked input finishes
The tested release serves all four exact current embedded assets
Patch peers require authenticated credentials and an accepted origin
Modern patches and legacy full snapshots converge on the exact Unicode text
Stale revisions, half-surrogates, range overflow, NUL and oversize inserts cannot change acknowledged text or history
Concurrent same-base patches acknowledge exactly one sender and preserve both peers revision fences
Patch generation and selected-project fences reject foreign writes while legacy edits remain supported
FileSync reads existing buffers without selecting files and cannot reopen a closed document
Every acknowledged patch survives an abrupt host exit and reconnect without modifying disk
Embedded Device drafts reaches inactive and deleted paths with at most thirty-two visible metadata rows
Downloading a deleted draft returns exact Unicode text without discarding its only saved copy or writing host files
Device draft discard requires explicit confirmation and frees only the chosen saved draft
A browser storage removal failure keeps a deleted draft recoverable through the same download action
limits: Frontend recovery proofs execute the actual function source in a controlled deferred-reply VM; Device drafts exercise exact embedded assets and real browser downloads.
This correctness fixture is not a latency or memory benchmark.
